Students will collaboratively design a training program tailored to the needs of a hospitality organization, incorporating principles of adult learning and industry-specific requirements.
Students will evaluate strategies for creating a positive workplace culture, improving employee motivation, and managing performance in hospitality and food service operations.

Students will analyze emerging workforce trends in the hospitality industry and develop strategies to address key workplace challenges, including the integration of technology, workplace ethics, and employee turnover.

objectives: By the end of this course, students will be able to describe how enduring personality traits and psychological characteristics influence a manager’s behavior and how these relate to and impact the organizational culture…
By the end of this course, students will be able to describe the role of managers in implementing strategy to achieve the goals and objectives of a hospitality organization.
By the end of this course, students will be able to describe the types of organizational structures that are appropriate in a hospitality setting.

By the end of this course, students will be able to describe how motivation theories can be applied in the hospitality context to maximize employee productivity, retention, professional development, and satisfaction.
By the end of this course, students will be able to explain leadership attributes contribute to the effectiveness of hospitality managers.
By the end of this course, students will be able to explain how effective group leadership contributes to the effectiveness of hospitality organizations.
By the end of this course, students will be able to describe how hospitality managers can encourage and facilitate collaborative cross-functional decision-making.
